apod.explanation: A crescent Moon and bright Venus appear together over Poland's Tatra Mountains at dusk in a planetary conjunction, with the bright star Spica — a triple star system about 250 light-years away in Virgo — just to Venus's left.
apod.title: Moon, Venus and Spica Meet

breaking.fact: Nvidia announced Thursday morning that founder-CEO Jensen Huang has resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, after the board met late Wednesday — reversing its Sunday statement of confidence in him. CFO Colette Kress, 59, is interim CEO while keeping her finance role, and director Harvey Jones, 73, becomes the board's first-ever chair. No reason was given in the 8-K filing. Shares fell as much as 14% early, then pared the loss to about 5% near $165 midday; earnings are due Nov 17.
breaking.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns effective immediately; Kress named interim chief

breaking.fact: Talks between Vladimir Putin and US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff ended in Moscow Thursday; Witkoff said 'progress was made,' the trilateral format has restarted and a new meeting is set, with European representatives possibly joining. Putin rejected any European troop presence in Ukraine after a deal and held to his demand that Kyiv surrender all of Donbas. The envoys now fly to Dublin to brief President Zelensky on Friday; the Abu Dhabi round agreed a major prisoner exchange but no ceasefire.
breaking.headline: Moscow talks end: envoys say progress made, trilateral talks restarted

breaking.fact: US existing-home sales fell 5.5% in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million — the lowest since August 2010 and below the 3.85 million consensus — as the average 30-year mortgage hit 7.33%, the highest since 2000 outside one month in 2023. Sales were down 8.8% year over year; inventory rose to 1.59 million homes, a 5.1-month supply, while the median price edged up 0.4% to $416,700.
breaking.headline: Existing home sales fall to 3.75 million, lowest since August 2010

breaking.fact: President Zelensky said Thursday that Starshield — the military-grade version of Starlink critical to Ukraine's military operations — has faced 'significant disruptions' in recent days, hampering Kyiv's ability to shoot down Russian drones. It is the latest recurrence of outages to the service, which Ukraine relies on for battlefield communications.
breaking.headline: Ukraine says Starshield hit by disruptions again as Moscow talks end

items.body: Iran's military said Thursday that four oil tankers have now been hit by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz: two supertankers carrying more than 4 million barrels combined were disabled late Wednesday after what Iran calls an unauthorised southern route — Iranian state media said they hit naval mines — and Iran's army said two more tankers hit mines Thursday afternoon in the eastern strait after disabling their radar. UKMTO separately reported a vessel hit by an unidentified projectile near Ras Al-Khaimah on Wednesday, causing an engine-room fire. Reuters could not verify Iran's account. At least 10 ships were hit in the first 10 days of November, after 37 attacks in October, per Washington Institute data.
items.headline: Four tankers struck by explosions in the Strait, Iran says

items.body: Kpler data reported by Reuters shows commercial cargo transits through the strait fell to 5 last Saturday, from 31 the week before, with none recorded Sunday, after ADNOC said three of its vessels were attacked; the IMO counts 133 confirmed incidents and 25 seafarer deaths since February, and is not advising ships to transit. Some vessels sail with AIS switched off, so the true count may be higher.
items.headline: Strait traffic collapses: 5 transits Saturday, none Sunday

hormuz.stats: Traffic & shares (latest verified): AIS-visible commercial traffic is running about 8% of normal — 6.9 ships a day over the past week (18 tankers) against 84.8 before the crisis. EIA puts Hormuz oil flows at 4.9M bbl/day in Q2 2026, down from 21.6M in Q4 2025; the IEA estimates ~20M bbl/day transited in 2025, about a quarter of global seaborne oil trade. China takes ~42% and India ~13% of strait crude throughput; ~90% of Iran's oil exports go to China. The EIA warns vessel-tracking data have become less reliable during the conflict.

marketsNote: Midday Thursday: stocks have rebounded from early losses after Nvidia's CEO resignation — S&P 500 +0.2% near 7,634, Nasdaq +0.1%, Dow +0.4% — as AMD and Broadcom jump ~6% and Alphabet gains ~3%, while Nvidia slides ~5% to ~$165. space.body: SpaceX is targeting Friday, Nov 13, for Starship Flight 15 from Starbase, Texas, in a 75-minute window opening at 4:45 PM CT — the first attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Ship upper stage in the launch tower's arms. Ship 42 would orbit about 14 times over 22-plus hours, deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites, and return for a tower catch Saturday afternoon; the flight is still pending an FAA license as of Nov 11.
space.headline: Starship Flight 15 targets Friday for first double tower catch

space.body: ESA's Euclid space telescope released its first major data batch, DR1 Foundation: 13 months of observations covering light from more than a billion objects across sky equal to 9,500 full moons, including over 900 million galaxies, around 15,000 strong gravitational-lensing candidates and more than 60 million quasar candidates. It lays the foundation for the largest-ever 3D map of the cosmos; the full Data Release 1 follows in mid-2027.
space.headline: Euclid releases best-ever 3D map of the universe

space.body: Flinders University scientists found that carefully controlled microscopic cracks boost an antibacterial coating of gallium-carbon nanotube film: after one minute of electrical stimulation from a standard 9-volt battery, more than 80% of MRSA and Pseudomonas aeruginosa cells were dead within three hours. The work, published in Small Structures, could lead to smart wound dressings and wearable devices that treat infections at the source.
space.headline: Tiny cracks and a 9-volt battery could help fight deadly superbugs

weekInBrief.body: October CPI rose 0.4% month over month, beating the 0.3% forecast, and CME FedWatch now puts a 25-basis-point December hike at 91% odds, up from 84% on Monday, with about 10% odds of a 50-point move. Fed Governor Waller backs a December hike and Dallas Fed President Logan says at least two more quarter-point rises are needed; the dollar index touched 103.02, its highest since April 2025. October PPI is due Friday at 8:30 AM ET, expected up 0.4% headline and 0.3% core.
weekInBrief.headline: December hike odds hit 91% as PPI looms Friday

weekInBrief.body: A day after CoreWeave's 25% surge revived the AI trade, Thursday's money rotated to Nvidia's rivals: AMD and Broadcom each jumped about 6% to lead S&P 500 advancers while Nvidia slid roughly 5% on Jensen Huang's resignation, and Alphabet gained about 3%. The split shows the AI trade alive but no longer a one-stock story.
weekInBrief.headline: AI money rotates: AMD, Broadcom jump 6% as Nvidia slides

weekInBrief.body: Anthropic's bankers are preparing to price its IPO above the $70-to-$78 range filed Tuesday after strong first-day roadshow demand, which could lift the valuation to $1.5 trillion or more, the Financial Times reported; the filed range implies $1.26-1.41 trillion fully diluted. Pricing is set for Nov 18 with Nasdaq trading Nov 19 under ticker ANT, alongside a $26 billion private placement from Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC — potentially the biggest IPO ever.
weekInBrief.headline: Anthropic IPO bankers weigh a $1.5 trillion valuation

weekInBrief.headline: Apple at a record high, up 31% in 2026
